observation_summary: The compiler fails to issue warnings for side-effect-free expressions when they appear as non-rightmost elements in a comma-separated expression sequence.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect traversal or validation logic within the compiler's side-effect checking pass. Specifically, the algorithm only checks the first element of a comma-separated sequence for side effects, ignoring subsequent non-rightmost elements. This is a procedural logic error in how the compiler analyzes expression trees, not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a check, the root cause is the algorithmic strategy of only inspecting the first element of a sequence rather than iterating through all non-rightmost elements.
